Crosswalk between boundary versions

Source: R/xw.R
bndxw.Rd

Carries values kept on one set of areas (the 158 neighbourhoods of a city's new boundaries, a census vintage's tracts) to another (the 140 old neighbourhoods) through a correspondence table: each link says what share w of a source area's value falls in a target area. Counts of a source wholly inside one target move whole (weight 1, exact); a source split between targets is shared by area or population (uniform density within the source, an assumption). The same table read the other way disaggregates. map also gives each source's main target, the column to add to a table keyed by the source areas.

Usage

bndxw(from, to, x, unit, w = NULL)

Arguments

from, to

The correspondence: the source and target area of each link, labels. A clpre list from clprep() is taken too (as from): its elements fill the arguments by name.

x

The values to carry: finite numbers, one per record.

unit

The source area of each record: labels (as in from).

w

NULL (every link weight 1), or the share of each link: numbers from 0.

Value

A list: tab, a data frame with one row per target (to, value); map, one row per source (from; to, the target of its largest share, the first of ties; share, that share; wsum, the sum of its shares, 1 when nothing is lost or counted twice); lost, the total of the records whose area is not in from; unmatched, those areas.

Examples

# old areas a, b merge into A; c splits between A and B by area
bndxw(from = c("a", "b", "c", "c"), to = c("A", "A", "A", "B"),
      x = c(3, 4, 5, 8), unit = c("a", "b", "b", "c"),
      w = c(1, 1, 0.25, 0.75))
#> $tab
#>   to value
#> 1  A    14
#> 2  B     6
#> 
#> $map
#>   from to share wsum
#> 1    a  A  1.00    1
#> 2    b  A  1.00    1
#> 3    c  B  0.75    1
#> 
#> $lost
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $unmatched
#> character(0)
#>
